summary: 31 runs in four families: H3/Quadbin cell utilities on Honshu epicenters (17), S2 cells (4), spherical geometry on Great Lakes shores (5) and planar joins on Great Lakes zones (6, including buffer selection and nearest joins). Most pictures are honest and legible, but 17 of 31 cards scrub a Data: or Simulated knob, and 9 scrub by full rebuild (resolution, k, level). Best posters are cell-rollup, cell-topology, point-in-polygon-join, spherical-convex-contains and buffer-selection. Worst are cell-geometry (fill by vertexCount is one flat color), s2-cell-hierarchy (48 overlapping seeds), hilbert-keys (random points hide the curve), s2-cell-measures (auto range turns a tiny latitude trend into a full ramp) and spatial-join-prepared (the prepared index is invisible). Several entries are near duplicates: cell-pyramid / cell-level-selection, cell-measures / s2-cell-measures, spherical-arc-overlay / spherical-polygon-overlay, spatial-predicate-join / spatial-join-candidates / spatial-join-prepared. The biggest lever is a shared 'pointer row' helper: append the pointer as one extra point to an existing per-frame positions buffer, so the real operation (GPUPointToCell, the joins, the contains tests) answers for the cursor on the GPU without a CPU H3/S2 port; this serves about 12 entries. Second lever: spherical-surveys.ts helpers taking a pointer longitude and latitude, so the five spherical runs become place/drag of their survey shapes. Third: join.ts drawing zone bounding boxes, so the join family explains candidates versus exact matches.

sharedChanges.change: Add addPointerCell(builder, family, resolution): a one-row positions buffer written per frame from the pointer, keyed with GPUPointToCell and decoded with GPUCellGeometry, returning the cell boundary for a highlight outline and the key for the readout. Lets cell runs probe without a CPU H3/S2 library.

Return zone bounding boxes (and bounds grown by a distance) as outline segments from uploadZones, and add a helper that appends one pointer row to a points buffer; candidates vs exact matches and the prepared index then become visible.

Let getSurveySwath take (longitude, latitude) and make every survey shape center a parameter, so the pointer's geographic position can move the operand in 2D; all five runs already rewrite these vertices per frame.

Give addPairSegments / addCsrEdgeSegments an optional highlighted left id (a one-word uniform) that writes a per-segment flag, so the hovered point's or zone's pairs can be drawn bright with no re-run.

frameworkNeeds: pointer position passed to update() in world and geographic (longitude, latitude via geographicWindow) coordinates, written per frame without a rebuild
2D pointer binding: x and y (or a lon/lat pair) drive two parameters or one vector input
cursor glyphs: ring of a radius in world or kilometer units, crosshair, box/polygon outline, a short tick from the cursor to the nearest feature
highlight one id on polygons, dots and lines layers (a highlight uniform compared against owners/values) for render-only probes
pointer to nearest dot / feature index lookup on CPU copies of inputs (stations, zones, seeds)
draw-time count from the pointer for paths (playhead along sortedRows)
snap-and-debounce for compile-time parameters (k, resolution, level) or pre-built variants, when a gesture must touch them
readout chip that can show an operation output value read back for the hovered element (count, area, key)
